annotations.title: Let me die with the Philisthiims.
annotations.text: [1] Manie thinges do iustifie Samsons fact in killing himself with the Philisthiims. First it appeareth by the miracle, that God directly and extraordinarily concurred by restoring in that moment his admirable streingth, that he could pull downe two such pillers. And conformably we may gather, that God inspired his mind to attempt this fact, and so he erred not, but obeyed God herein, as S. Augustin noteth. li. 1. c. 21. & 26. de ciuit. Dei. Secondly he was moued with zele of Gods honour, hearing the Idolaters praise their false god Dagon. Thirdly, he had a good and pure intention to reuenge him selfe for Gods more glorie, praying to him for restauration of streingth. Fourthy he did not directly desire to kil himselfe, but to kil the Philisthims, though himselfe must also die with them. [2] And in this act especially he was a figure of Christ, who chiefly by his death conquered his enemies.

notes.text: Samson excused in killing himselfe with his enemies.
